exclusion_rationale.summary: Hall stands convicted of kidnapping and is serving life without parole. He has never been charged with or convicted of homicide in any jurisdiction. No cause of death was determinable in the case for which he was convicted, and no body has been recovered in any other case attributed to him. He is widely described as one of the most prolific offenders in American history on the strength of confessions he has recanted and which investigators have been unable to corroborate. He therefore cannot enter the offender roster, where he would contribute an unproven victim count to every aggregate computed from this dataset.

judicial_findings.value: The Seventh Circuit in 1996 held that expert testimony on false confessions had been wrongly excluded and vacated the conviction, ordering a new trial. On remand that expert evidence was admitted after a Daubert analysis, the jury convicted, and the 1999 panel affirmed.

judicial_findings.notes: Both directions matter. A federal appellate court found the confession evidence required expert scrutiny; a jury then heard that scrutiny and convicted anyway. Accounts that cite only one half misrepresent the record.

cause_of_death_determination.value: None. The body was recovered approximately six weeks after the disappearance and had been severely damaged by farm machinery; cause of death could not be determined.

sources.citation: United States v. Hall, 93 F.3d 1337 (7th Cir. 1996)

cause_of_death_determination.notes: Decisive and almost universally omitted. Popular accounts state a method of killing; the record establishes that no method could be determined. Hall's statement asserted strangulation — an assertion the forensic evidence could neither confirm nor contradict, which is one of the reliability problems the appellate court identified.

homicide_attribution.value: Investigators have publicly suspected Hall in roughly nineteen further disappearances beyond Jessica Roach. No charge has followed in any of them. In the 1992 Laurie Depies disappearance, officials declined to charge him, citing his record of retracted admissions and the absence of physical evidence.

sources.citation: Bustle. 'Suspected Black Bird Serial Killer Larry Hall Was Never Charged With Murder.' 2022.

homicide_attribution.notes: Recorded as what investigators suspect, which is a fact about the investigation, not about Hall. Suspicion sustained over decades without charge is itself the datum.

victim_count_claims.value: Figures of 'up to 40' and '40 to 50' circulate widely. They originate in expert commentary to news media and in Hall's own retracted admissions. No agency has published an attribution figure with a stated methodology.

corroboration.notes: The absence of corroboration is the reason no further charges have been brought, and the reason the circulating victim totals cannot be recorded as counts.

reliability_findings.value: The Seventh Circuit identified specific problems: Hall asserted the victim had been strangled although no cause of death could be established; his apparent knowledge of where the body lay tracked the fact that the questioning officer came from that area; he placed the date within a four-day range; and the statement contained nothing genuinely incriminating that investigators did not already possess. Defence experts testified that a personality disorder left him pathologically eager to please interrogators.

sources.citation: United States v. Hall, 93 F.3d 1337 (7th Cir. 1996)

reliability_findings.notes: These are the appellate court's own observations, not a defence submission. That distinction matters: this is not a fringe challenge to a settled conviction.

identifying_evidence.value: No physical evidence. The case against Hall rested on his statement and on identification evidence.

sources.citation: United States v. Hall, 93 F.3d 1337 (7th Cir. 1996)

interrogation_method.value: Approximately seventeen hours across two sessions, unrecorded, with the statement written out by the interviewing agent.

sources.citation: United States v. Hall, 93 F.3d 1337 (7th Cir. 1996)

interrogation_method.notes: Contemporaneous best practice now requires full electronic recording of custodial interrogation in serious cases, precisely because an unrecorded interrogation cannot be reviewed.

other_suspects.value: Hall sought at retrial to introduce statements by two other men implicating them in the offence. The evidence was excluded and the exclusion was upheld on appeal.

other_suspects.notes: The two men are named in the published opinion. This dataset does not repeat their names: they were never charged, and reproducing them here would extend an accusation beyond the court record's own context.

method_now_disputed.value: Eyewitness identification evidence was relied on, and expert testimony on identification reliability was excluded. The research consensus since has been that identification evidence is substantially more error-prone than lay intuition assumes.

research_value.why_recorded: This case sits at the exact point the dataset exists to examine: a man convicted on an unrecorded confession, in a case with no physical evidence and no determinable cause of death, who is nonetheless described publicly as one of the most prolific killers in American history on the strength of admissions he retracted and nobody could corroborate. It is simultaneously a study in confession reliability, in the gap between attribution and proof, and in how a television dramatisation becomes a citation. It also demonstrates why the offender roster and the case file must be separate: recorded as an offender with forty victims, this subject alone would distort every aggregate the dataset supports.
